Margin formula

Gross margin = (1 - COGS - commission) x Sales - salary x employees, i.e. 0.45 x Sales - 3.00 x employees, with salary Rs. 3.00 L per employee per month and commission 5.0% of sales.

6.Productivity & Diminishing Returns

Productivity summary

Diminishing returns detected: Yes. Capacity-optimum headcount: 9.

Reading the headcount optimum

The optimiser searches the headcount range the store has actually operated (plus one hire) and treats the marginal contribution as constant, so a persistently positive marginal pushes the answer to the top of that range. The scenario comparison answers the practical question -- hire one, wait, or hold -- under an explicit ramp-up curve.

9.Business Rule

Recommended business rule

Adaptive Staffing Rule: Maintain a 3-month rolling average of sales per employee. If the rolling average exceeds Rs.16.48 L, hire one additional employee. If it falls between Rs.12.79 L and Rs.16.48 L, hold current headcount and replace departures. If it drops below Rs.12.79 L, do NOT replace departing staff. Optimal target headcount based on historical margins: 7 employees.

Rolling-average trigger
MetricValue
Window (months)3
Hire above16.48
Hold band12.79 to 16.48
Do not replace below12.79
Current rolling average14.51
Threshold-based decision rules
ConditionAction
sales_per_emp >= 17.60HIRE an additional employee.
11.88 <= sales_per_emp < 17.60HOLD current headcount.
sales_per_emp < 11.88DO NOT replace departing employee.

Why this beats 'always replace'

  • The 'always replace' rule ignores current sales levels. During low-sales months the extra salary erodes margin.
  • The adaptive rule ties staffing decisions to actual revenue performance, avoiding unnecessary costs in lean months and scaling up when the market supports it.
  • Run `backtest_staffing_rules` for the measured backtested saving rather than an assumed percentage.

Backtest interpretation

Replaying both policies over 81 months, the adaptive rule produced Rs.3.00 L of gross margin (0.1%) more than always replacing, and avoided overstaffing in 17 month(s) (21 % of the period).

10.Appendix

Business assumptions

  • Customer traffic and footfall remain stable.
  • No significant hiring or recruitment costs are incurred.
  • No training-period productivity loss beyond the modelled ramp-up (70% -> 100% over 6 months).
  • Monthly salary stays fixed at Rs. 3.00 Lakhs per employee.
  • Commission remains fixed at 5.0% of total sales.
  • Cost of goods sold stays at 50% of sales.
  • Economic conditions and consumer demand remain similar.
  • No major competitor entry or exit during the projection period.
  • Store operating hours remain unchanged.
  • The pricing and assortment strategy remains consistent.
  • Sales are treated as exogenous: the analysis prices staffing decisions against realised demand.
